link.title: Inferential Statistics & Hypothesis Testing
link.description: Inference is reasoning from a limited sample back to the population that generated it — and honestly quantifying how sure you're allowed to be. This module works one lecture at a time: the mindset (the null/alternative framing, the p-value, the two ways to be wrong), the tests for a mean (the z-test when σ is known, the Student-t distribution and t-test when it isn't, choosing between them, and the confidence interval), the categorical tests (chi-square goodness of fit), ANOVA (comparing the means of three or more groups), and Bayesian reasoning (Bayes' theorem and the base-rate trap). Every page has an interactive lab or a visual and a runnable example. (Study reference: the 'Inferential Statistics' section of a Complete Data Science bootcamp — all notes, code, and visuals are my own.)
